challenge.better_approach: Looked: (a) gitignore the lab, rejected because the lab is committed on purpose so one folder can be carried to a bare machine and regrow the system (CLAUDE.md); (b) every box stashes before pulling, rejected as policy not physics (Law 4). Committing what the gate writes is the smallest change that keeps the lab tracked.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That two boxes' compiles are byte-identical (the diff shows only added charter fields, no host paths); if a compile embeds a host-specific value, committing it from every box would conflict. The proof must measure identical bytes across two scratch roots.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: commits titled 'lab recompiled' (93ac32844, 43e479621 in the commons) show the lab is committed by hand after a recompile, and recompile_gate.sh install (ticket f09cd0588ceb) already pokes the gate on merge. Read cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh; no ticket found for the dirt itself.
challenge.real_collision: None found: the 'derived, never authored' rule allows several derived writers and the gate committing its own output stays a derived write; Law 7 is kept because a failed commit is recorded, not swallowed.

answers.falsifier: After charters skills/note, commit, challenge gained runtime_role and gated_by (a8d9ded2f, a61009024), a post-merge recompile on akiendell left 3 modified lab files in the commons; once fixed, the same sequence in a scratch tree leaves `git status` clean and a `pull --ff-only` succeeds.
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a measured bug: akiendell 2026-11-19, a commons pull aborted on lab files; see cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh and the lab file intentions-congruency-lab/skills-note--intention+why.json in CairnCommons
answers.how: recompile_gate.sh (the lab's write gate, intentions_model_compiler) leaves the lab it regenerated committed in the commons in the same act through the artifact/commit door, so the post-merge recompile and the /sorted write-through stop producing tracked dirt; red-first proof over a scratch commons + code root. First-cut, a hypothesis to measure: byte-identical regeneration on two boxes merges without conflict.
answers.traces_to: Law 5 (the thing and the story of the thing may live in two roots but may never contradict each other: a stale committed lab contradicts its charters) and the 'lab is derived, never authored' bug in CLAUDE.md (ticket the-lab-is-derived-never-authored); Law 9 (nothing is green that is built, running and inspected).
answers.what: A charter change and its compiled lab copy reach the commons together, so the derived intentions-congruency-lab never sits as uncommitted tracked dirt that aborts a commons pull on every box.

bullets.text: The lab drifts after a charter change because the recompile (post-merge hook, /sorted write-through) regenerates it into the working tree and nothing commits it; the next pull --ff-only on that box aborts. Measured on akiendell 2026-11-19 with 3 skills charters.
Whether the gate or a post-commit step should commit the lab is a CC-answerable hypothesis, measured by the byte-identical-across-boxes tooth; it is not a question for Akien.
